structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E011. The tip is E010: Muon (Newton-Schulz with 3 steps already in the code), Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30%, batch 2000, last group at 512, and the epoch count in the code is 9.5. It scores 6.64 s at 0.7548, which is only 0.18 pp above the 0.753 bar and below my ~0.756 safety bar for the 40-seed judgment.

Measured prices (time cost per pp of accuracy):
- Compile plus fused SGD: −14% time (E004). A recompile leak costs about +3 s (E003).
- EMA/Lookahead: about +1 pp for roughly zero time (E005). This is the largest free gain so far.
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time for −0.59 pp (E007), about 3.5 s per pp. This was a good trade.
- Aggressive resizing 20/24/28/32 (E011): −1.3 s for −1.4 pp versus E007, about 0.9 s per pp. That is a bad trade, worse than epochs. Accuracy loss grows super-linearly once the 32-px tail is ≤20% and 20 px is used. The time saving was bigger than I forecast: small resolutions do not lose as much GPU efficiency as I assumed. I now treat time as roughly proportional to the pixel fraction.
- Epochs: about 2 s per pp near 9 epochs (E008).
- Width 576→512 (E010 vs E007): −0.69 s for −0.43 pp, about 1.6 s per pp.
- LR decay to 0 on top of EMA: noise (E009).

Budget: time ≈ F + V × pixel fraction. F is about 0.5-0.8 s (H2D, pad, whitening, Lookahead setup, per-epoch augment/interpolate/permute copies). V is about 7.5 s at full resolution. Steps take ~28 ms each, about 235 in total. GPU compute dominates. Launch overhead is probably 3-6% under the 4-CPU pin: fwd/bwd, Muon and fused SGD are three separate compiled regions with Python-float LRs and Python Lookahead. CUDA graphs or break removal can therefore win at most about 0.2-0.4 s, and they carry implementation risk.

Accuracy levers left untested: LS 0.2, Muon LR, wd, BN recalibration. My prior is that none is worth ≥0.3 pp, because the airbench values are already close to tuned. wd mostly touches the SGD groups, since Muon renormalizes the filter norms, so the wd lever is weak. The real way to buy margin is epochs, at ~2 s per pp. The tip is fragile: if the 40-seed offset is negative, we need +0.25 epoch (≈+0.2 s).

Noise: compiled runs are deterministic per seed. Per-seed std is about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Recipe reshuffles move the mean by up to ~0.3 pp. Time noise is about 1-2%.

Misses:
- I keep underestimating accuracy gains from known-good airbench components.
- I underestimated the time saved by small resolutions.
- I overestimated the accuracy kept under aggressive resizing.

Unsure about:
- the offset between seeds 0-2 and the 40-seed mean;
- the true launch-overhead fraction;
- whether plain EMA without the fast-weight reset matches Lookahead;
- whether the I020 change is a no-op (the code already uses 3 Newton-Schulz steps).

forecasts.reason: GPU-bound steps of ~28 ms leave about 3-6% launch overhead, and Muon, SGD and Lookahead partly sit outside the graph, so the gain lands near the 3% threshold.
Diagnostic only. I expect the 10-seed mean within ±0.3 pp of 0.7548 and a std of about 0.25 pp.
Label smoothing near its optimum is flat. With 100 classes, 0.3 is not obviously too high, so a ≥0.3 pp gain is unlikely.
With norm-fixed weights the LR sets the angular step, and ×1.5 is just as likely to hurt as help over short runs.
Muon renormalizes the filters, so wd only reaches the BN biases and the head. It is a weak lever.
The code already runs 3 Newton-Schulz steps, so this is likely a no-op: identical accuracy and time within noise.
A few host syncs or breaks probably exist, but the run is compute-bound, so removing them gains about 1-3%.
The Lookahead reset also smooths the trajectory, so I expect plain EMA to land about 0.2-0.4 pp lower, close to the 0.3 pp threshold.

cruxes: What is the offset between the seeds 0-2 mean and the 10/40-seed mean for E010? If it is negative, the tip must buy back roughly 0.25 epoch before any time cut counts.
What fraction of a training step is GPU-idle under the 4-CPU pin? Above about 8% makes CUDA graphs and break removal worthwhile; below 3% makes them pointless.
Is there any accuracy lever (BN recalibration, LS, Muon LR, plain EMA) worth ≥0.3 pp at zero time? Only such a gain would fund a further width or resolution cut, which costs about 1.6 s per pp.
